beats.care: Don't reply YES or NO to unknown bank messages. Block, delete, and check your bank app directly. If cheated, call 1930 fast.
beats.what: Hyderabad police commissioner V.C. Sajjanar warned of WhatsApp messages from unknown numbers saying money was debited, then asking you to reply NO.
beats.why: He says replying can trigger a hidden malicious file that gives scammers control of the phone. A chartered accountant was recently cheated this way.

cards.body: Police call it an 'auto-execution file attack'. They say victims didn't share an OTP or click a link. Banks don't ask customers to confirm transactions over WhatsApp.
Fear makes people act fast. A message saying money just left your account pushes you to respond before you think.
cards.title: why do scammers fake a debit?

cards.q: How do you treat messages from unknown numbers?

opts: Check your bank app directly, don't reply
cards.q: WhatsApp says money left your account. What should you do?
cards.why: Your bank app shows real transactions; replying to unknown numbers is exactly what scammers want.

hook: A WhatsApp says reply *'NO'* to stop a debit. Don't.

learn.t: Scammers fake debit alerts to cause panic. The safe check is opening your own bank app, never replying to the message.

sources.name: Siasat
sources.title: WhatsApp message reply can wipe out savings, warns Sajjanar

tldr: Hyderabad police chief V.C. Sajjanar warned that replying 'NO' to fake WhatsApp debit messages from unknown numbers can let scammers drain your account.
